Leak Detection in Lakewood Ranch, FL

Quick answer: Leak detection in Lakewood Ranch, FL often starts in the yard. Large lots, long service lines, big irrigation systems and pools add a lot of buried pipe. A local pro isolates each system with valve tests, then uses acoustic tools and tracer gas to pinpoint the leak in plastic pipe.

Lakewood Ranch is a master-planned community that spans about 35,000 acres in southeastern Manatee County and northeastern Sarasota County. It runs roughly from State Road 64 in the north to Fruitville Road in the south, with Interstate 75 on its western edge. The Braden River flows through the southern part. The 2020 census counted about 35,000 residents in the census-designated place.

Why leaks in Lakewood Ranch are different

The land was once the Schroeder-Manatee Ranch, used for cattle and timber for decades. The planned community grew after Interstate 75 arrived, so most homes are newer than in the older coastal towns. That changes the kind of leaks people see.

Newer homes usually have plastic water lines, such as PEX or CPVC. Plastic is quiet, so a leak in it doesn't hiss as loudly as copper. Lots are often larger, so service lines and irrigation runs are long. Many homes have pools, outdoor kitchens and lake views, all with their own buried pipes.

The community also crosses a county line. Some homes are in Manatee County and some are in Sarasota County. Your utility, permits and building office depend on which side you are on.

Tips for Lakewood Ranch homeowners

  • Learn your irrigation shut-off. Closing it during a meter test is the fastest way to tell a sprinkler leak from a service line leak.
  • Keep the builder's plans. Plumbing and irrigation drawings from the builder can save hours of line locating.
  • Test after landscaping work. New fence posts, palms and pavers are a common cause of nicked lines. Read the meter after any digging.
  • Know which county you're in. It decides who to call for leaks at the meter and which office issues permits.

Quiet leaks in plastic pipe

A leak in PEX or CPVC can be hard to hear with a ground microphone, especially under deep sod or pavers. That's where tracer gas helps. The line is drained, a safe gas is pushed in, and a sensor finds where it rises through the soil. Line locating maps the pipe path first, which matters when lines curve around pools and beds.

Before any digging, Florida requires a call to Sunshine 811 at least two full business days ahead. Communities with buried power and fiber need careful marking.

HOA and community rules

Many Lakewood Ranch neighborhoods have rules for digging, lawn repair and contractor access. Check with your association before a repair that opens the front yard or a shared area. The provider can usually plan the job to limit visible damage.

New-home warranty and builder questions

If your home is only a few years old, check your builder's warranty before paying for a repair. Some plumbing defects may still be covered. Keep the warranty papers, your closing documents and any builder plumbing plans together. When you call, mention the home's age and builder. A provider can tell you whether what they find looks like a defect, wear or outside damage, which helps you decide who to contact next.

Leak detection in Lakewood Ranch: questions

Do you cover all of Lakewood Ranch?

Calls from across Lakewood Ranch in ZIP codes 34202, 34211, 34212 and 34240, on both the Manatee County and Sarasota County sides, can be connected with local providers.

How do I tell if my irrigation system is leaking?

Close the irrigation shut-off valve, then watch the water meter with all fixtures off. If it stops, the leak is likely in the irrigation system.

Can newer homes have slab leaks?

Yes. Poor installation, kinked lines and pipe rubbing against concrete can cause slab leaks in homes of any age.

Will a leak repair damage my landscaping?

Pinpointing the leak first keeps digging to a small area. The provider can explain how sod and pavers will be put back.
